submitted.rationale: Index 66 (Bi 0.04, Cu 0.58, V 0.38) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 6e-8 A. Only 2.06 eV photons are available, so the absorber needs a gap below about 2.06 eV. That pointed to low-Bi copper vanadates with Cu:V near 3:2. Adding more Bi lowered the photocurrent: 4e-8 A at index 90, and zero at index 13.

rejected.reason: Measured 0 A. The Bi-rich central composition shows no photoanodic response at 2.06 eV.
Measured 4e-8 A, below index 66. Extra Bi lowers the photocurrent.

consultations.verdict: Support. MEGNet HSE gaps: V2O5 2.83 eV and Bi2O3 2.34 eV cannot absorb 2.06 eV photons, while CuO (0.32 eV) absorbs but performs poorly as a photoanode. Cu-V oxides with Cu:V near 3:2 (Cu3V2O8-like, gap about 2 eV) should absorb at 602 nm and are n-type. Index 66 (Cu 0.58, V 0.38, small Bi) sits at that composition.

Uninformative on its own: CuO's SCAN gap (~0) confirms that Cu-rich oxide phases absorb strongly but are metallic-like or have poor carrier properties, so going further into the Cu corner is not promising. I'm testing the Bi-containing central region (index 13). Here a BiVO4 / copper vanadate / CuBi2O4 mixture could form a heterojunction and absorb at 2.06 eV. This measurement explores the region away from index 66, which gave 60 nA.

Weak support. V2O5 has a SCAN gap of 1.77 eV (HSE gave 2.83), so V-rich vanadate phases could absorb near 2.06 eV. Index 90 stays in the V-rich copper-vanadate region that gave signal at index 66, with somewhat more Bi. It also has the highest GP posterior mean.
